headline: Luka Doncic powers the Lakers past the Hawks, stretching the win streak to 6
text: ATLANTA -- — Luka Doncic had 32 points, eight rebounds and 10 assists and the Los Angeles Lakers extended their winning streak to six games with a 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks on Monday night. Walker Kessler had 21 points and 10 rebounds, and Collin Sexton had 18 points and six assists off the bench. The Lakers were without guard Austin Reeves, who missed the game due to illness one day after scoring 43 points at Detroit. Sandro Mamukelashvili scored 23 points and was 5 of 8 from 3-point range. The Lakers as a team shot 43% from beyond the arc (15 of 35). CJ McCollum led the Hawks with 21 points off the bench. Nickeil Alexander-Walker had 20 points and Oneka Okongwu had 16 for Atlanta, which saw its winning streak end at four games. Dyson Daniels was the primary defender on Doncic, and he also had 10 points, eight assists, four steals and a rare 3-pointer. The Hawks pulled cut the Lakers lead 115-111 on a Daniels bucket with 3:30 to play, but a 6-0 burst by the Los Angeles put the game out of reach. Doncic had a driving layup and an assist during the run. The Lakers built a 20-point lead in the second quarter as they sliced through the Hawks defense repeatedly. Doncic set up teammates with eight first-half assists and Kessler had three easy alley-oop dunks off Sexton drives to the basket. The Hawks recovered late in the half with some improved shooting and cut the deficit to nine at the break. Lakers rookie Cameron Carr had a two-handed dunk in transition in the first quarter for his first career points. Up next Lakers: At Milwaukee on Wednesday night. Hawks: At Chicago on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Grayson Allen scores 27, Naz Reid adds 25 as Hornets beat Cavaliers 124-112 to snap 6-game skid
text: CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- — Grayson Allen scored 27 points, Naz Reid added 25 points and 13 rebounds and the Charlotte Hornets beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 124-112 on Monday night to snap a six-game losing streak. Tidjane Salaun added 14 points off the bench and Ryan Kalkbrenner had 15 rebounds for Charlotte, which shot 23 of 46 from 3-point range. Charlotte built a 33-point lead in the third quarter then hung on to win after the Cavaliers cut the lead to 118-110 with four minutes left. Meleek Thomas led the way for the Cavaliers with 18 points. The Hornets came into the game ranked second to last in the league in 3-point field goal percentage at 28.8%, but hit 12 of 24 from deep in the first half to build a 16-point halftime lead. Allen, Reid and Salaun combined for 52 of Charlotte’s 69 points before the break. Eager for their first win since Oct. 26, the Hornets stayed hot in the third quarter and extended the lead to 33 with Sion James knocking down three key 3s. He finished with 11. Cavaliers coach Kenny Atkinson chose to play his reserves the entire fourth quarter even after his team trimmed the lead to single digits. But the Cavaliers couldn't get any closer than eight and Royce O'Neale 's 3 from the right wing with 2:40 left in the game pushed the lead to 13. It was a big win for the Hornets. who played without starters Brandon Miller (hip strain), Kon Knueppel (hamstring) and Moussa Diabate (quadriceps). Peyton Watson added 13 points and Jared Allen had 12 for the Cavs. James Harden and Donovan Mitchell each had 11. Up next Cavaliers: At New York on Wednesday night. Hornets: At Phoenix on Thursday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Collins puts up 24 points and 10 rebounds as Pistons beat Davis and Wizards, 122-111
text: DETROIT -- — John Collins had 24 points and 10 rebounds as the Detroit Pistons beat the Washington Wizards 122-111 on Monday at Little Caesars Arena. The Pistons overcame a 44-point, 13-rebound performance from Anthony Davis , who had been a game-time decision because of an ankle issue. Daniss Jenkins finished with 22 points and eight assists after moving into the starting lineup. Jenkins scored a career-high 31 points in Sunday's loss to the Los Angeles Lakers . Duncan Robinson scored 22 for Detroit. AJ Dybantsa scored 21 points for Washington, which lost its fourth straight. Trae Young had 20 points and seven assists. The Pistons led by 10 at the half and shot 63.2% from the floor in the third quarter. Jenkins had 13 points in the quarter as Detroit extended the lead to 103-87. Cade Cunningham didn't return until midway through the fourth quarter after picking up a fifth personal foul in the third, but the Pistons had built a comfortable 115-99 lead. Davis, who set the scoring record at the Palace of Auburn Hills with a career-high 59 points for the Pelicans in 2016, started the game like he was headed toward breaking Anthony Edwards ' Little Caesars Arena record of 53. He finished with 30 points in the first half on 10 of 11 shooting — making both of his 3-point attempts and 8 of 9 attempts from the free-throw line. But he didn't get much help. Young scored 13 points in the half, but the other three starters combined for 14 points and the bench added just one point. Meanwhile, the Pistons had three starters in double figures — Robinson, Collins and Cunningham — and got 19 points from the reserves. Up next Wizards: At Indiana on Wednesday before hosting Detroit on Thursday. Pistons: At the Washington on Thursday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Jerome scores 27 points as Grizzlies improve to 5-0 on road by routing short-handed Raptors 118-102
text: TORONTO -- — Ty Jerome scored 27 points, Cameron Boozer added 22 and the Memphis Grizzlies improved to 5-0 on the road this season by beating the short-handed Toronto Raptors 118-102 on Monday night. Memphis is the only NBA team without a road loss this season. They’ve also won at Golden State, Sacramento, Utah and Portland. Jerami Grant scored 17 points and Jaylen Wells had 14 as the Grizzlies snapped a three-game losing streak and won for the fifth time in six trips to Toronto. Boozer had seven rebounds and eight assists. Zach Edey had eight points and nine rebounds in his lone regular-season visit to his hometown. Memphis was without center Isaiah Stewart (right knee) for the second straight game. Grizzlies center Quinten Post left in the first quarter after being elbowed in the face while defending Jamison Battle’s drive to the basket. Jamal Shead had 20 points and 11 assists for the Raptors, who played without three starters. Kawhi Leonard (left knee) missed his sixth straight game, while Scottie Barnes (left groin) and Immanuel Quickley (right hamstring) each sat for the second straight. The Raptors were also without reserve forward Collin Murray-Boyles , who sat out because of an illness. RJ Barrett scored 19 points for Toronto. Battle and Jakob Poeltl each had 18 and Ja’Kobe Walter added 12. The Raptors won their opening two games of the season but haven’t won back-to-back games since. Up next Grizzlies: Host Denver on Wednesday night. Raptors: Host Boston on Wednesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Flagg has 43 points, 10 rebounds, Irving 35 points in Mavericks' 125-122 win over Pacers
text: DALLAS -- — Cooper Flagg had 43 points and 10 rebounds and Kyrie Irving scored 35 while completing a back-to-back for the first time this season as the Dallas Mavericks rallied past the Indiana Pacers 125-122 on Monday night. P.J. Washington Jr. could have extended the Dallas lead with four seconds left but missed both free throws, with Indiana’s Obi Toppin grabbing the rebound. The Pacers’ final possession ended with Dallas’ Caleb Martin tipping away a pass by Andrew Nembhard near the sideline. Pacers coach Rick Carlisle expressed his displeasure with the game officials at midcourt that a Dallas foul wasn't called. Flagg had a season-high in scoring while Irving tied for his season best. They combined to score 26 points in the fourth quarter — including Dallas’ first 13 — as the Mavericks outscored the Pacers 35-29. Irving, in action this season after missing 19 months with a torn ACL, played 28 minutes in Sunday night’s 130-93 rout of Brooklyn and a season-high 38 minutes against Indiana after sitting out the second game of the Mavericks’ first back-to-back 2½ weeks ago. He hit a season-high seven 3-pointers. Dallas (7-4) swept a three-game homestand and is three games over .500 for the first time since March 1, 2025 (at 32-29). Flagg has four straight double-doubles and five this season. The Pacers (3-8) were led by Pascal Siakam with 29 points, but only three of those were scored in the second half. Aaron Nesmith scored 18 points with two of his four 3-pointers coming in the final minute. Siakam hit 8 of 9 from the floor during the first half, including 5 of 6 behind the arc, plus 5 of 6 from the line for 26 points. He was the lone Pacer in double figures in building a 13-point lead that was 66-56 at halftime. Up next Pacers: Host Washington on Wednesday. Mavericks: At Minnesota on Thursday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Durant and Sengun power the Rockets past the Nuggets 110-100 to snap a 2-game skid
text: HOUSTON -- — Kevin Durant had 23 points and Alperen Sengun added 20 to lead the Houston Rockets to a 110-100 win over the Denver Nuggets on Monday night that snapped a two-game skid. Denver's Jamal Murray made two free throws to cut the lead to six points with about five minutes left. But Christian Braun missed a pair of free throws after that and Houston got baskets from Sengun and Amen Thompson to push the lead to 100-90 with four minutes remaining. The Rockets got back on track after losing to Minnesota and Phoenix following a 7-1 start to the season. Murray had 38 points in his fourth game this season with at least 34 points as Denver’s two-game winning streak ended. Nikola Jokic added 25 points and had 16 rebounds and eight assists. Four quick points by Murray, with the help of a turnover by Sengun, got the Nuggets within four points with less than seven minutes to go. But a short basket by Sengun followed by a 3-pointer from Fred VanVleet extended Houston’s lead to 96-87 with 5 1/2 minutes remaining. The Rockets had a 16-point lead early in the third quarter before the Nuggets used an 18-2 run to tie it at 60-60 with about five minutes left in the quarter. Jokic, Murray and Cameron Johnson all made 3-pointers to power that run while the Rockets missed nine consecutive shots and had two turnovers. Their only points in that stretch came on a pair of free throws by Durant. Houston got its first field goal in more than 6 1/2 minutes on a basket by Tari Eason with about four minutes left in the third. That was the start of an 11-2 run that made it 71-62. Up next Denver visits the Grizzlies on Wednesday night. The Rockets host Golden State Wednesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Wembanyama has 40 points, 9 blocks as Spurs win 9th straight with 122-96 victory over Suns
text: PHOENIX -- — Victor Wembanyama scored 40 points, grabbed 11 rebounds and blocked nine shots in another dominant performance to help the San Antonio Spurs beat the Phoenix Suns 122-96 on Monday night. The Spurs have now won nine straight games after dropping their first two contests of the season. The Suns had no answer for the 7-foot-4 Wembanyama, who controlled the game at both ends of the floor, particularly during the first half. The two-time All-Star had 22 points, six rebounds and five blocks before the break as the Spurs used a 21-2 run to take a 61-46 halftime advantage. Dylan Harper scored 14 of his 17 points in the third quarter to help the Spurs extend their lead 93-68, which allowed the starters to sit for much of the fourth. Wembanyama finished 15 of 19 from the floor, including 2 of 3 from beyond the arc and needed just 25 minutes on the floor to do his damage. De'Aaron Fox added 15 points while Julian Champagnie and Harrison Barnes both had 11. It's the second time in four games that Wembanyama has had a massive stat line during an MVP-worthy run to start the regular season. He had career highs of 52 points and 24 rebounds in a 112-111 win over the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday and might have approached those numbers against the Suns if he had played more. Devin Booker led the Suns with 32 points on 10 of 17 shooting. Khaman Maluach was the only other player who scored in double figures with 11 points. The Suns shot just 39.3% from the field and were outrebounded 55-35. They have a 2-2 record on their current seven-game homestand. Up next Spurs: At Chicago on Wednesday night. Suns: Host the Los Angeles Clippers on Tuesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski each score 25 as Warriors run away from Pelicans for 138-87 win
text: SAN FRANCISCO -- — Stephen Curry scored 25 points in 20-plus minutes, Yaxel Lendeborg had 23 points, seven rebounds and four assists, and the Golden State Warriors won their eighth straight game by running away from the undermanned New Orleans Pelicans early for a 138-87 victory Monday night. Brandin Podziemski added 25 points while Curry wound up 6 for 10 with four 3-pointers coming off a 41-point performance in Saturday’s 126-119 overtime win against Orlando. He passed DeMar DeRozan (26,800) for 16th place on the NBA's career scoring list with 26,803. Golden State had three players with at least 20 points for the second time this season and the Warriors finished with 30 or more assists — 37 — for the third straight game and fifth in the last six. They are 6-0 when doing so. Injured guard Jimmy Butler dressed up like a member of the coaching staff and held a clipboard, writing “PASS TO STEPH” on it. Golden State guard Brandon Williams injured his left hamstring and was scheduled for an MRI exam, according to coach Steve Kerr. Derik Queen scored 16 points off the bench and Dejounte Murray added 12 points for the Pelicans, who were out of the game almost from the tipoff and trailed 72-43 at halftime on the way to losing a third straight after a four-game winning streak. Golden State led 35-20 after one quarter as New Orleans shot just 7 of 23 and missed 10 of 12 3-point tries. The Warriors built a 23-point lead early in the second as Podziemski scored four quick points and rolled from there. Charles Bassey contributed 12 points and 10 rebounds off the bench and De'Anthony Melton scored 16 with four 3s. Lendeborg and Pelicans guard Jordan Poole , both former Michigan stars, traded jerseys afterward. New Orleans rested Zion Williamson a night after a 139-123 road loss to the Clippers and Trey Murphy III also sat out to manage his troublesome knees after he scored 26 in Los Angeles on Sunday. The Warriors lost second-year guard Will Richard to a torn ligament in his left thumb and the team said he would weigh his options over the next week on whether to have surgery or wear a splint while playing. Up next Pelicans: Host Brooklyn on Wednesday night. Warriors: At Houston on Wednesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
